meta.subject: English
meta.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood
meta.title: Rubric Check: Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which sentence keeps active voice in both clauses and uses the present subjunctive for a hypothetical situation?
choices: The manuscript is revised by the editor, and the author rewrites as if she was a novice.
The editor revises the manuscript, and the author rewrites as if she were a novice.
The editor revises the manuscript, and the author rewrites as if she was a novice.
The manuscript is revised by the editor, and the author rewrites as if she were a novice.
questions.explanation: The first option uses active voice in both clauses and the subjunctive "were" for a contrary‑to‑fact condition.
questions.skill: Maintaining Consistent Voice and Mood
questions.topic: Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A formal medical recommendation must use the present subjunctive in a that-clause after suggests. Which sentence meets the rubric?
choices: The physician suggests that the patient reduces the dosage.
The physician suggests that the patient reduce the dosage.
The physician suggests that the patient reduced the dosage.
The physician suggests that the patient is reducing the dosage.
questions.explanation: In a formal that-clause after suggests, the present subjunctive uses the base form reduce.
questions.skill: Using the present subjunctive in a that-clause
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires active voice in the main clause and passive voice in the relative clause, without identifying the writer. Which sentence meets it?
choices: The teacher gave the students feedback, which was written by the students.
The teacher gave the students feedback, which they wrote in their notebooks.
The feedback was given to the students, which was written on their papers.
The teacher gave the students feedback, which was written on their papers.
questions.explanation: The sentence keeps the main clause active, makes the relative clause passive, and leaves the writer unidentified.
questions.skill: Creating a voice shift within a relative clause
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A process description must shift from active voice in the first clause to passive voice in the second, with both clauses in the present tense. Which sentence follows the rubric?
choices: The technician entered the sample, and it was placed in the incubator.
The technician enters the sample, and it places the sample in the incubator.
The sample is entered by the technician, and the technician incubates it.
The technician enters the sample, and it is placed in the incubator.
questions.explanation: The first clause uses active present-tense voice, while the second uses passive present-tense voice with the actor unstated.
questions.skill: Locating a deliberate active-to-passive shift
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check): Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which sentence maintains active voice in both clauses?
choices: The librarian cataloged the books and returned them to the shelves.
The librarian cataloged the books, while the shelves were cleaned.
The books were cataloged by the librarian, and she returned them to the shelves.
The books were cataloged by the librarian, and the shelves were cleaned by the staff.
questions.explanation: The librarian is the subject and the actor of both cataloged and returned, so the sentence maintains active voice throughout.
questions.skill: Checking voice consistency
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires a present subjunctive in an active that-clause after urge, with receive as the verb. Which sentence meets the requirement?
choices: The coach urges that each player receives clear feedback.
The coach urges that each player receive clear feedback.
The coach urges that each player received clear feedback.
The coach urges that each player be given clear feedback.
questions.explanation: After urges, the present subjunctive uses the base form receive, and the active clause makes the player the grammatical subject.
questions.skill: Checking present subjunctive in active that-clauses
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) — Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires passive voice with ought to in the first clause and active voice with will in the second. Which sentence meets both requirements?
choices: The application ought to be submitted by Friday, and the confirmation will be given by the registrar.
The application ought to submit by Friday, and the registrar will confirm it.
The application ought to be submitted by Friday, and the registrar will confirm it.
The application ought to be submitted by Friday, and the registrar confirms it.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses passive voice with ought to in the first clause and active voice with will in the second clause.
questions.skill: Applying voice and modal requirements across clauses
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A blog post must shift from first-person plural narration to a direct second-person command. Which sentence makes that shift correctly?
choices: We have reviewed the evidence, so compare the dates yourself.
We have reviewed the evidence, so you should compare the dates yourself.
We have reviewed the evidence, so let us compare the dates ourselves.
We have reviewed the evidence, so the dates should be compared by you.
questions.explanation: The opening is first-person plural, and compare the dates yourself is a direct second-person imperative.
questions.skill: Shift person and mood deliberately
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A stage direction must shift from third-person active narration to first-person passive narration, with both actions in the simple past. Which sentence fits the rubric?
choices: The director arranged the lights, and I was called backstage.
The director arranged the lights, and I called someone backstage.
The director was arranging the lights, and I was called backstage.
The director arranged the lights, and was I called backstage?
questions.explanation: Arranged is third-person active, and was called is first-person passive, with both verbs in the simple past.
questions.skill: Shifting from third-person active to first-person passive narration
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A safety instruction must use a present-tense declarative warning followed by an imperative command. Which sentence follows the rubric?
choices: The trail was flooded, and cross the bridge instead.
The trail is flooded, and cross the bridge instead.
The trail is flooded, and the bridge should be crossed instead.
The trail is flooded, and we crossed the bridge instead.
questions.explanation: The warning is declarative and present tense, while cross the bridge instead is an imperative command.
questions.skill: Distinguish declarative and imperative mood
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which sentence consistently uses a first-person point of view?
choices: She checked the map, and I trusted the marked trail.
I checked the map, and she pointed to the marked trail.
I checked the map, and I trusted the marked trail.
They checked the map, and we trusted the marked trail.
questions.explanation: This sentence consistently refers to the narrator with the first-person pronouns I and we can be avoided entirely by using I in both clauses.
questions.skill: Checking point-of-view consistency
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A museum audio guide must move from a second-person imperative to a second-person interrogative, with both actions in the present tense. Which sentence fits the rubric?
choices: Read the bronze plaque, and do you know why the artist dated it?
Read the bronze plaque, and did you know why the artist dated it?
You read the bronze plaque, and do you know why the artist dated it?
Read the bronze plaque, and you do know why the artist dated it?
questions.explanation: Read is an imperative verb, and do you know is a present-tense interrogative addressed to the listener.
questions.skill: Shifting from imperative to interrogative mood
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A diary entry must move from second-person imperative narration to first-person past-tense narration without an unwarranted shift. Which sentence fits?
choices: Lock the file before you leave, and I save a copy yesterday.
Lock the file before you leave, and saved a copy yesterday.
The file should be locked before you leave, and I saved a copy yesterday.
Lock the file before you leave, and I saved a copy yesterday.
questions.explanation: The sentence shifts from the second-person imperative Lock the file to first-person past narration in I saved a copy yesterday.
questions.skill: Checking shifts in person, tense, and mood
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires a factual present-tense conditional with present indicative in the if-clause and will in the result clause. Which sentence meets it?
choices: If the library opened early, more students would arrive.
If the library opens early, more students will arrive.
If the library were to open early, more students will arrive.
If the library opens early, more students might arrive.
questions.explanation: The sentence presents a real possibility with the present-tense form opens and uses will for the result.
questions.skill: Distinguishing factual and hypothetical conditionals
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires an indicative main clause and a present subjunctive in the that-clause. Which sentence uses the required mood?
choices: The judge requires that each witness speaks clearly.
The judge requires that each witness spoke clearly.
The judge requires that each witness will speak clearly.
The judge requires that each witness speak clearly.
questions.explanation: The bare verb form speak expresses the present subjunctive required after requires that.
questions.skill: Distinguishing indicative and subjunctive clauses
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A narrator must use present indicative in the independent clauses and a past subjunctive in the as-if clause. Which sentence follows this pattern?
choices: The engine idles in the garage, and it sounded as if it were asleep.
The engine idles in the garage, and it sounds as if it is asleep.
The engine idles in the garage, and it sounds as if it were asleep.
The engine idles in the garage, and it sounds as if it be asleep.
questions.explanation: Idles and sounds are present indicative forms, while were asleep is the past subjunctive used in the as-if clause.
questions.skill: Shifting from indicative to subjunctive mood
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires passive voice in both clauses and the same past-perfect tense throughout. Which sentence meets both requirements?
choices: By noon, every application had been reviewed, and a winner had been chosen.
By noon, every application was reviewed, and a winner had been chosen.
By noon, every application had been reviewed, and the committee chose a winner.
By noon, every application was reviewed, and a winner was chosen.
questions.explanation: Both clauses use passive voice with the past-perfect construction, and the action was completed by noon.
questions.skill: Checking voice and tense consistency against a rubric
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which sentence fulfills a rubric that demands a third‑person passive clause in the past perfect tense followed by a first‑person active clause in the simple past?
choices: The documents had been filed by the clerk, and I have reviewed them yesterday.
The documents were filed by the clerk, and I reviewed them yesterday.
The documents had been filed by the clerk, and they were reviewed by me yesterday.
The documents had been filed by the clerk, and I reviewed them yesterday.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence begins with a past perfect passive clause and shifts to a first‑person simple past active clause.
questions.skill: Shifts in Voice and Mood
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires active voice in the first clause, passive voice in the second, and a present subjunctive in the that-clause after recommends. Which sentence meets all three requirements?
choices: The director recommends that each performer changes costumes, and the new outfits are fitted before rehearsal.
It is recommended that each performer change costumes, and the new outfits are fitted before rehearsal.
The director recommends that each performer change costumes, and the new outfits are fitted before rehearsal.
The director recommends that each performer change costumes, and the costume staff fit the new outfits before rehearsal.
questions.explanation: The first clause is active, change is the present subjunctive after recommends, and are fitted makes the second clause passive.
questions.skill: Apply a combined voice and mood rubric
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires passive voice in both clauses using the past perfect tense. Which sentence satisfies the rubric?
choices: By the deadline, the report had been submitted, and the data had been analyzed.
By the deadline, the report had been submitted, and the team analyzed the data.
By the deadline, the report was submitted, and the data had been analyzed.
By the deadline, the report had been submitted, and the data has been analyzed.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses past perfect passive 'had been submitted' and 'had been analyzed' in both clauses.
questions.skill: Evaluating sentence compliance with voice and mood rubric
questions.topic: Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires active voice in the first clause, passive voice in the second, and the present perfect tense in both. Which sentence meets all three requirements?
choices: The technician checked the device, and the alarm was reset.
The technician has checked the device, and the alarm has been reset.
The technician had checked the device, and the alarm was reset.
The device has been checked by the technician, and the technician has reset the alarm.
questions.explanation: The first clause uses active present-perfect voice with has checked, and the second uses passive present-perfect voice with has been reset.
questions.skill: Checking a voice-and-tense rubric
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check): Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires passive voice and simple past tense in both clauses. Which sentence meets both requirements?
choices: The clerk sorted the letters, and a courier delivered the packages.
The clerk sorted the letters, and the packages were delivered.
The letters were sorted, and a courier delivered the packages.
The letters were sorted, and the packages were delivered.
questions.explanation: Both letters and packages serve as subjects of passive verbs in the simple past tense.
questions.skill: Checking passive voice and tense consistency
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A narrator must begin with first-person active narration, then shift to third-person passive narration, keeping both clauses in the simple past. Which sentence meets every requirement?
choices: I unlocked the studio, and the instruments were tuned before dawn.
The studio was unlocked by me, and the instruments were tuned before dawn.
I unlocked the studio, and I tuned the instruments before dawn.
I unlocked the studio, and the instruments tuned themselves before dawn.
questions.explanation: The first clause is first-person active, the second is third-person passive, and both use simple past tense.
questions.skill: Check first-person and third-person voice
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A writer wants the past subjunctive in an as-if clause. Which sentence uses that form correctly?
choices: The child frowned as if the answer were wrong.
The child frowned as if the answer was wrong.
The child frowned as if the answer is wrong.
The child frowned as if the answer will be wrong.
questions.explanation: The past subjunctive form were expresses a condition presented as contrary to fact in the as-if clause.
questions.skill: Using the past subjunctive in an as-if clause
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric calls for active voice in the first clause and passive voice in the second. Which sentence follows that pattern?
choices: The coach reviewed the plan, and the team revised it before practice.
The coach reviewed the plan, and the team was informed before practice.
The coach was informed of the plan, and the team revised it before practice.
The plan was reviewed by the coach, and the team revised it before practice.
questions.explanation: The first clause uses active voice, while the second uses passive voice to emphasize the information received by the team.
questions.skill: Applying a rubric for a purposeful voice shift
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A records policy must use present tense and active voice in the main clause and a passive subjunctive in the requests that-clause. Which sentence meets the rubric?
choices: The director requests that each file is archived before closing.
The director requests that each file be archived before closing.
The director requests that each file archive before closing.
The director requested that each file be archived before closing.
questions.explanation: Requests is the present active main verb, and be archived is a passive subjunctive in the requests that-clause.
questions.skill: Using a passive subjunctive in a that-clause
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric calls for an indicative main clause followed by a present subjunctive in a that‑clause after insists. Which sentence follows this pattern?
choices: The director insists that the actor rehearses the scene again.
The director insists that the actor rehearse the scene again.
The director insisted that the actor rehearsed the scene again.
The director insists that the actor should rehearse the scene again.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses indicative 'insists' and the present subjunctive 'rehearse' in the that‑clause.
questions.skill: Evaluating sentence compliance with voice and mood rubric
questions.topic: Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Identify the sentence that fulfills a rubric demanding a consistent first‑person perspective, active voice, and the subjunctive mood for a wish.
choices: I draft the report, and I wish the deadline was later.
The report is drafted by me, and I wish the deadline was later.
I draft the report, and I wish the deadline were later.
The report is drafted by me, and I wish the deadline were later.
questions.explanation: The first sentence stays in first person, uses active voice, and employs the subjunctive "were" for a wish.
questions.skill: Maintaining Consistent Voice and Mood
questions.topic: Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A recipe instruction should name the cook in the first clause but shift to passive voice in the second, leaving the helper unstated and keeping both clauses in the present tense. Which sentence follows that rubric?
choices: The cook chops the onions, and the mixture is stirred for five minutes.
The onions are chopped, and the cook stirs the mixture for five minutes.
The cook chops the onions, and the cook stirs the mixture for five minutes.
The cook chops the onions, and the mixture will be stirred for five minutes.
questions.explanation: The first clause uses active voice to identify the cook, while the second uses passive voice, leaves the helper unstated, and remains in the present tense.
questions.skill: Identifying purposeful active-to-passive shifts
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) — Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires a simple past indicative main clause and a past subjunctive in an as‑if clause. Which sentence meets the requirement?
choices: She stares at the painting as if it were alive.
She stared at the painting as if it was alive.
She stared at the painting as if it were alive.
She stared at the painting as if it had been alive.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses simple past 'stared' and the past subjunctive 'were' in the as‑if clause.
questions.skill: Evaluating sentence compliance with voice and mood rubric
questions.topic: Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which sentence meets a rubric calling for a conditional with a present subjunctive in the if‑clause and a future indicative in the result clause, both in active voice?
choices: If the manager approved the plan, the project would launch.
If the manager approves the plan, the project will launch.
If the manager approve the plan, the project will launch.
If the manager had approved the plan, the project would have launched.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence employs the present subjunctive form in the if‑clause and a future indicative in the main clause, both in active voice.
questions.skill: Shifts in Voice and Mood
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which sentence satisfies a rubric that calls for a shift to passive voice in the second clause only, while keeping the subjunctive mood for a contrary‑to‑fact condition in both clauses?
choices: If the committee met, they would review the proposal.
If the committee met, the proposal would be reviewed by them.
If the committee were to meet, they would review the proposal.
If the committee were to meet, the proposal would be reviewed by them.
questions.explanation: The first option uses the subjunctive "were to meet" in the if‑clause and shifts to passive voice in the result clause as the rubric specifies.
questions.skill: Maintaining Consistent Voice and Mood
questions.topic: Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which sentence satisfies a rubric that requires a passive first clause in the future perfect tense followed by an active second clause also in the future perfect tense?
choices: By next year, the report will be completed, and the team will present the findings.
By next year, the report will have been completed, and the team will have presented the findings.
By next year, the report will have been completed, and the findings will have been presented by the team.
By next year, the report has been completed, and the team presented the findings.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence uses a passive future perfect construction in the first clause and an active future perfect construction in the second clause.
questions.skill: Shifts in Voice and Mood
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires passive voice in the first clause and active voice in the second. Which sentence meets those requirements?
choices: The analyst entered the data, and she checked them for errors.
The data were entered, and the errors were checked by the analyst.
The data were entered, and the analyst checked them for errors.
The data were entered by the analyst, and the errors were checked for completeness.
questions.explanation: The first clause is passive because the data are the subject of the action, while the second is active because the analyst performs the checking.
questions.skill: Shifting from passive to active voice
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires a present subjunctive in a that-clause after proposes. Which sentence meets the requirement?
choices: The senator proposes that the committee delay the vote.
The senator proposes that the committee delays the vote.
The senator proposes that the committee delayed the vote.
The senator proposes that the committee would delay the vote.
questions.explanation: The present subjunctive uses the base form delay in the that-clause after proposes.
questions.skill: Applying present subjunctive in a that-clause
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive conditional with a conditional perfect result?
choices: If the committee has reviewed the proposal, it would have approved it.
If the committee had reviewed the proposal, it would approve it.
If the committee reviewed the proposal, it would have approved it.
If the committee had reviewed the proposal, it would have approved it.
questions.explanation: Had reviewed establishes the unreal past condition, while would have approved expresses the expected perfect result.
questions.skill: Matching conditional forms
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A speaker regrets being unable to attend an earlier concert. Which sentence expresses that regret with the subjunctive mood?
choices: I wish I would attend the concert yesterday.
I wish I have attended the concert yesterday.
I wish I would have attended the concert yesterday.
I wish I had attended the concert yesterday.
questions.explanation: Had attended is the past subjunctive form that expresses regret about not attending the earlier concert.
questions.skill: Use the subjunctive for a past regret
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which revision best passes a rubric requiring consistent active voice and a consistent hypothetical subjunctive?
choices: The team practiced every evening, and the coach praised them for the effort. If the players were more patient, they would improve.
The team practiced every evening, and the coach praised them for the effort. If the players were more patient, they will improve.
The team practiced every evening, and they were praised for the effort by their coach. If the players were more patient, they would improve.
The team practiced every evening, and the coach was praised for the effort. If the players were more patient, they had improved.
questions.explanation: This revision keeps both first-sentence predicates active and uses were with would to maintain the hypothetical subjunctive in the second sentence.
questions.skill: Revising shifts in voice and mood
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires passive voice with the modal can. Which sentence meets the rubric?
choices: The committee can approve the proposal after the vote.
The proposal can be approved after the vote.
The proposal will be approved after the vote.
The proposal can receive approval after the vote.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses the modal can with the passive construction can be approved.
questions.skill: Applying a voice-and-mood rubric
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric demands a past perfect subjunctive in the if‑clause and a conditional perfect in the result clause, both in active voice. Which sentence fulfills the rubric?
choices: If the engineer had tested the circuit, the system would have been functioning properly.
If the engineer tested the circuit, the system would have functioned properly.
If the engineer had tested the circuit, the system would function properly.
If the engineer had tested the circuit, the system would have functioned properly.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses past perfect 'had tested' in the if‑clause and conditional perfect 'would have functioned' in the result clause, both active.
questions.skill: Evaluating sentence compliance with voice and mood rubric
questions.topic: Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A spotlight requires a passive first clause and an active second clause, with the same person serving as the agent in both. Which sentence meets the rubric?
choices: Lena wrote the song, and it was performed by Lena at the festival.
The song was written by Lena, and Lena performed it at the festival.
The song was written by Lena, and the performance by Lena featured it.
The song was written by Lena, and Lena was performed at the festival.
questions.explanation: The first clause is passive, while Lena performed it is active and identifies Lena as the agent in both clauses.
questions.skill: Check passive-to-active voice consistency
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric calls for active voice in the first clause and passive voice in the second, with the second actor unstated and both clauses in simple past indicative mood. Which sentence meets it?
choices: The clerk stamped the forms, and a courier sealed the envelopes.
The forms were stamped, and the envelopes were sealed.
The clerk stamped the forms, and the envelopes were sealed.
The clerk stamped the forms, and the envelopes were sealed by a courier.
questions.explanation: The first clause is active, while the second uses the simple past passive without naming the actor.
questions.skill: Applying a controlled active-to-passive shift
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires active voice in both independent clauses and the modal would in both clauses. Which sentence meets the rubric?
choices: The coach would explain the rule, and the questions would be asked by the visitors.
The rule would be explained, and the visitors would ask questions.
The coach would explain the rule, and the visitors would ask questions.
The coach would explain the rule, and the visitors ask questions.
questions.explanation: This sentence keeps both clauses active and uses the modal would with a base verb in each clause.
questions.skill: Applying a voice-and-modal rubric
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the subjunctive mood correctly for an unreal present condition?
choices: If the road was flooded, we would take the bridge.
If the road were flooded, we would take the bridge.
If the road were flooded, we will take the bridge.
If the road were flooded, we had taken the bridge.
questions.explanation: The form were with would correctly presents the flooded road as an unreal condition and the bridge crossing as its expected result.
questions.skill: Checking subjunctive mood
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9: Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires active voice in the first clause and passive voice in the second clause, both in simple past tense. Which sentence meets the requirement?
choices: The architect designs the building, and the construction is completed on schedule.
The architect designed the building, and the construction completed on schedule.
The building was designed by the architect, and the construction was completed on schedule.
The architect designed the building, and the construction was completed on schedule.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses active past 'designed' in the first clause and passive past 'was completed' in the second clause.
questions.skill: Evaluating sentence compliance with voice and mood rubric
questions.topic: Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A rubric requires the present subjunctive in a that-clause after recommends. Which sentence follows the rubric?
choices: The committee recommends that the designer revises the logo.
The committee recommends that the designer should revise the logo.
The committee recommends that the designer revise the logo.
The committee recommends that the designer revised the logo.
questions.explanation: The bare present-tense verb revise expresses the present subjunctive required after recommends.
questions.skill: Checking subjunctive mood against a rubric
questions.topic: Write Your Own (Rubric Check): Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A profile must use active voice in the main clause and passive voice in the nonrestrictive relative clause. Which sentence meets the rubric?
choices: The curator unveiled the archive, which is housing the documents in a converted bank.
The curator unveiled the archive, which housed the documents in a converted bank.
The archive was unveiled by the curator, which housed the documents in a converted bank.
The curator unveiled the archive, which was housed in a converted bank.
questions.explanation: Unveiled is active, and was housed is a passive verb in the nonrestrictive relative clause.
questions.skill: Shifting voice between a main clause and a relative clause
questions.topic: Activity 7 of 9 (quiz/game): Write Your Own (Rubric Check) - Shifts in Voice and Mood

questions.prompt: A process description must use active voice with will in the first clause and passive voice with will in the second, leaving the second actor unstated. Which sentence follows the rubric?
choices: The scouts will mark the trail, and the maps will be posted before sunrise.
